notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 2 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Brayden Schenn takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L3. Tony DeAngelo is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Hutton and Kessel.
Mathew Barzal is out (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Ben Hutton was added to the roster on Nov 6 and has played beside Matthew Kessel.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, down from 37% last season.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Tyson Hinds has not dressed for the last 6 games. Travis Mitchell has taken his spot beside Tristan Luneau. That pair has had 27% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 37:04 together, down from 62% with Hinds.
Troy Terry returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Laurent Brossoit was added to the roster on Nov 3.

story.head: Old-time hockey
paras: The Islanders won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 on Long Island on Oct 20. The Islanders (8-6-4) beat Los Angeles 5-2 on Thursday, while the Ducks (10-8-1) lost 4-2 to Nashville on Wednesday. Going in, the Isles are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Ducks third in the Pacific (tied for 16th).

The Islanders’ record (.556) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.473), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Ducks’ (.553 on chances worth .496), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and spread the ice time through the lineup (2nd). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Ducks’ not so much. As for the Ducks, they forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st). Anaheim has allowed 3.68 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (2nd), so expect plenty of it.

Bo Horvat (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (6 G / 12 A / 18 P in 18 GP) shares it. For the Ducks, Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against the Islanders. Cutter Gauthier (16 G / 7 A / 23 P in 18 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games.

Ilya Sorokin (7-4-2 / .915 SV% in 13 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and will likely start. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .866 SV% in 10 GS). Brossoit has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
